novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new across-token phenomenon and measurement: an LLM may "commit to an answer token distribution several positions BEFORE its internal retrieval of the relevant fact has completed," quantified through a "retrieve-vs-commit gap." Searches for "LLM premature answer commitment retrieval timing," "future-token decoding hidden states," "answer commitment across autoregressive positions," and "pause tokens before answering" indicate that the closest precedents are Future Lens: Anticipating Subsequent Tokens from a Single Hidden State (Pal et al., 2023) and Think Before You Speak: Training Language Models With Pause Tokens (Goyal et al., 2024), which respectively decode future tokens from hidden states and provide extra computation before output, but do not posit or measure a mismatch between fact-retrieval time and answer-commitment time. Moving from those works to this claim is a substantive natural extension and multi-step integration—rather than a mere object substitution—but the core tools and commitment-delay concept combine established future decoding, probing, and pause/deliberation ideas rather than introducing an entirely new interpretability paradigm.
